newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA - SHKELE INSISTS BALANCED BUDGET POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA - SHKELE INSISTS BALANCED BUDGET POSSIBLE.

text.p: Outgoing Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Friday that a balanced budget was possible this year and that moves to have a budget deficit were due to "pre-election populism" bu ruling parties.
"It is totally new to me that the balanced budget is impossible," he told a news conference.

"If we could mend a funding gap of 70 million lats in one year (1996) and if we have a 35 million lat surplus in the first half of 1997, then I do not believe that we are unable to cover a 22 million lat shortage," he added.
"This is not a matter of not being able to do so but obviously of not being willing to do," he added.
"Understanding that 1998 is a pre-election year we might expect 'political' salaries and 'political' pensions," he added.

"I understand that political populism is an unavoidable thing...but it should not be allowed to destory previous achievements. Noone doubts the correctness of the current framework which we have achieved," he added.
Finance Minister Robert Zile said on Thursday that the 1997 budget may have a deficit of 10 to 12 million lats due to lower-than-expected tax collection.
